lines.text: Parabolas and quadratics are everywhere on the SAT. Let's master vertex shifts and the discriminant in sixty seconds.
Start with y equals x squared at zero, zero. Vertex form is a times x minus h squared, plus k.
Watch the sign trap! x minus three shifts the vertex right to positive three, and minus four drops it down to negative four.
How many times does it cross the x axis? Check the discriminant: b squared minus four a c. Right now it crosses twice: D is positive, two real roots.
Slide the vertex right onto the x axis, and the two roots merge into one! D equals zero.
Lift it above the x axis, and it never touches at all: D is negative, zero real solutions.
Now here is a classic SAT problem: for what value of c does y equals x squared minus six x plus c touch the x axis at exactly one point?
One point means D equals zero! Negative six squared is thirty-six, minus four c equals zero. Four c is thirty-six, so c equals nine!
Practice this right now in the Functions quiz inside SAT Math Learner.
